analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Cross Asset / Consumer Outlook / Earnings 10 Nov 2026
key_insights: US equities closed higher on solid volumes: SPX +235bps to 7549, all 11 sectors up, 423 stocks up, VIX -22.31% to 19.92, Tech +4.42%, Industrials +3.52%, Comm Svs +2.49%. DJIA +215bps to 52389, NDX +274bps to 25253 despite NVDA -4.3%, with SOX +6.85%.
Crude fell about 5% to $85 on further Iran de-escalation, which helped sentiment.

In Europe, AI names (EU Semis GSSBSEMI +4.82%) and Italian banks (GSXEITBK +4.65%, after Credit Agricole/BAMI M&A and strong UCG earnings) outperformed. EU Cyclicals vs Defensives (GSPECYDE) rose 2.2%, with long-only buying in RR, LN, AIR FP, ASML NA and SAP GY.
US Info Tech net allocation is 14.4% of total US net market value, in the 1st/1st/3rd percentiles on 1-year/3-year/5-year lookbacks.
During last week's selloff retail bought the dip. Leveraged ETFs took record inflows of +$3.3bn on Thursday. SOXL attracted +$5.1bn in 5-day net inflows, and TQQQ, SNXX, GDXU and NVDL also benefited.

Flow was a mix of covering and long buying across Tech yesterday (ex-NVDA on weekend headlines). The market is hesitant to call the all clear ahead of CPI today (GIR at +16bps for core MoM) and CRWV/NBIS earnings later this week. Floor activity was 5 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers were flat with demand in tech and financials vs supply in comm services. HFs were net buyers, driven by macro products.

Cross-asset: GS remains overweight equities over 3m/12m on earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations, but overweight cash near term because of AI and Middle East uncertainty. Three paths to a risk appetite rebound: easing AI concerns with monetisation signs, rates relief helped by lower energy prices, and a larger decline of the RAI below -1.

US consumer outlook: GS expects consumer spending to grow 2.2% in 2027 (Q4/Q4). A softer start is expected as higher rates weigh on durables, energy prices stay elevated and nonprofit spending falls after the midterms. A pickup follows as inflation pressure abates and tax refunds and the reversal of benefit cuts turn the fiscal impulse modestly positive.

US semis: GS favors NVDA and AVGO, which imply no growth from 2027. In semi cap equipment it sees 2027 WFE as a baseline and prefers AMAT and LRCX. Memory is approaching oversold levels as it moves toward tangible book.

Rheinmetall CEO fireside (Buy, PT EUR2100, 7x EBITDA): management is confident the Arminius programme will proceed, artillery ammunition outlook is supportive, and it sees a naval pipeline across new-build, maintenance and ship repair, with strong demand across vehicles, ammunition, air defence, naval and emerging technologies.

Infineon Q4 and Q4/FY27 guidance came in line. Data center guide near EUR4B is ahead of the sellside but below the buyside's >EUR4B. GS calls the FX guide conservative, and notes management tends to guide to numbers it can beat.

Sunrise Q3 was in line with the street and guidance was reiterated. Pluxee was upgraded to Neutral from Sell (PT EUR12.20) after share price underperformance and another reset of earnings expectations.

earnings_insights: Infineon Q4 (reported): revenue EUR4.71B in line, EBIT EUR1.12B vs consensus est EUR1.10B, margin 23.8% vs consensus est 23.3% and guidance of about 23%. Q4 and FY27 guidance in line. Data center guide near EUR4B is ahead of the sellside, below the buyside's >EUR4B.

Sunrise Q3 (reported): revenue CHF732m in line with the street, adjusted EBITDA aL beat by 0.3% at CHF264.8M, OFCF beat on lower capex, FCF missed on working capital. Adjusted FCF CHF32.5M vs year-ago CHF36.7M. FY26 guidance confirmed.
CRWV and NBIS report earnings later this week (per the note).
